t: You're standing in Bloomsbury Square, a garden square in Bloomsbury, in the London Borough of Camden. It was developed in the late seventeenth century and was first called Southampton Square, which makes it one of the earliest squares in London. Bedford House once stood along the north side, but by the early nineteenth century it had been pulled down and replaced with terraced housing designed by James Burton. Several people connected to the square are named in the records. Edmund Lodge, a herald and writer on heraldry, died here and is buried here. Sir Robert Eyre, a judge who became Chief Justice of the Common Pleas, also died here.
